headline: Seven Dead in NovaMind BCI Trials — Families Demand Halt to 'Brain Gambling'
body: Seven trial participants have died and nineteen remain in critical care following the latest round of NovaMind's BCI implant trials conducted at a Helix Biosystems-affiliated clinic in The Circuit, according to internal adverse event reports leaked to this outlet. The deaths, which NovaMind attributes to 'pre-existing neurological vulnerabilities incompatible with first-generation integration protocols,' occurred between May 3rd and June 9th — a span the company did not disclose publicly. Families of the deceased, most of whom were low-income residents of The Narrows recruited with a 1,500 quanta participation stipend, have formed the advocacy group Minds Not Markets and are demanding a Federal Remnant moratorium on further trials. 'My brother signed a form he couldn't fully read because the consent interface ran through an early-build BCI he'd been given to test,' said Kwame Reyes-Oduya, 28, brother of victim Noel Reyes-Oduya. 'That's not consent. That's a trap.'
aftermath: NovaMind suspended public trial disclosures but continued testing under a reclassified 'internal research' designation, eventually producing the Mark II implant in 2107 — which carried a mortality rate of under 0.3 percent and became the standard foundation for all BCI technology in GLMZ.
runner_relevance: The leaked adverse event reports became one of the most sought-after documents in The Circuit's early runner economy — Minds Not Markets offered 6,000 quanta for authenticated originals, while NovaMind simultaneously contracted runners to identify and neutralize the leak source. This created a rare double-contract situation where competing teams were chasing the same data in opposite directions. Medical smuggling contracts also emerged as bereaved families sought unregistered neural surgeons in The Underworld to remove improperly installed trial implants from surviving participants.
